items.text: Can explain what WAF is and why it's not a service but a framework
Can name all 6 WAF pillars from memory (OSRPCS)
Can define each WAF pillar with a real-world analogy
Can explain what CAF is and when it's used
Can name all 6 CAF perspectives from memory
Can clearly explain the difference between WAF and CAF
Can explain why network hardening and system hardening are both needed
Can identify which WAF pillar applies to a given scenario (e.g., server crash → Reliability)
Can identify which CAF perspective is relevant for a given stakeholder (e.g., CISO → Security)
Can distinguish between network hardening and system hardening examples
Can identify the 4 components of network hardening architecture
Can explain the Principle of Least Privilege with an example
Can answer: WAF has 6 ___ (pillars), CAF has 6 ___ (perspectives)
Can answer: WAF is used ___ migration (after), CAF is used ___ migration (before/during)
Can identify Sustainability as the newest WAF pillar added in 2021
Can map CAF roles correctly (CISO → Security perspective, CTO → Platform perspective, HR → People perspective)
Know that port 22 (SSH) from 0.0.0.0/0 violates network hardening
